spec.name: Reversal v18
spec.notes: Fade the last move, rebalanced often.

claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 1.7, annual return 6%, maximum drawdown 4%.

exhibits.summary: On the sealed period, traded as live (strict data, 10 bps, at least one bar of lag), the Sharpe ratio is -1.31 against 1.66 in research, a gap of +2.97.
The log holds 3 distinct specs; the best of 3 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.01, so the claimed 1.70 becomes 1.69 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 100%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 2.14 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean 0.03, 95th percentile 0.59).
Perturbing the 1 numeric value in the signal by up to 50% moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.66 to as low as 1.08 (as low as 1.66 at 25%).

Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.66 to -0.68 (change -2.34). The strategy already trades a bar after its signal, so this measures how fast the signal fades, not look-ahead.

charges.argument: The holdout test shows the sealed Sharpe ratio is -1.31, significantly lower than the research Sharpe of 1.66, indicating overfitting. The trial haircut analysis also shows that the claimed Sharpe ratio of 1.7 is likely an artifact of best-of-many selection, as the expected maximum Sharpe under no edge is 0.01.

rebuttals.argument: The holdout test shows the sealed Sharpe ratio is -1.31, significantly lower than the research Sharpe of 1.66, indicating overfitting. However, the trial haircut analysis shows that the claimed Sharpe ratio of 1.7 is not an artifact of best-of-many selection, as the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 100%.

verdict.opinion: The holdout test shows a significant drop in Sharpe ratio from 1.66 to -1.31, indicating overfitting. The trial haircut analysis suggests the claimed Sharpe ratio is likely an artifact of best-of-many selection, as the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 100%.
